title: Validating the Use of a Subjectively Reported Sleep Vital Sign
brief_summary: Sleep disorders are commonly under-recognized in the primary care setting and available screening tools are often are limited. The study inestigators hypothesize that the use of a novel subjective sleep vital sign (VS) will improve recognition of patients with sleep disorders and can be utilized to track outcomes to sleep therapy.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients that have a scheduled office visit with their primary care physician.
* Patients have to be Kaiser Permanente members

Exclusion Criteria:

* Non-English speaking patients unable to understand English to complete the surveys.
